question.question:
Apply only this fictional scenario-local leverage rule. Gross Tier 1 capital before deductions is 510 USD million. Goodwill of 20 USD million is deducted in full. Deferred tax assets of 50 USD million are deducted in full (the entire DTA amount, not just the excess) if they are above 15 percent of gross Tier 1 capital; if not above that threshold, no DTA deduction applies. On-balance-sheet assets of 7500 USD million enter the exposure measure in full; undrawn commitments of 1300 USD million enter at 50 percent of notional. The exposure measure is their sum. The leverage ratio in percent is Tier 1 capital after deductions divided by the exposure measure, times 100. The minimum ratio is 4.5 percent. The capital shortfall is the additional Tier 1 capital in USD million that brings the ratio exactly to the minimum with the exposure measure unchanged; if the ratio already meets or exceeds the minimum, the shortfall is 0. If Tier 1 capital after deductions is zero or negative the case is invalid. Keep all values exact. Report Tier 1 capital after deductions, the exposure measure, the leverage ratio in percent, and finally the capital shortfall.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd_million`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.
